en.headline: Chinese medicine lab cuts velvet-antler test to under a day
en.dek: The Department of Health institute says a DNA method can show whether Lu Rong slices are authentic in less than a day, down from three.
body: The Department of Health’s Government Chinese Medicines Testing Institute has completed 22 thematic research projects since it was set up in 2017, including a rapid DNA method for checking whether Lu Rong, or velvet antler, slices come from genuine sources, the government said on Sunday.

Under the Chinese Pharmacopoeia, only antlers from sika deer or red deer count as authentic Lu Rong; material from other species is treated as an adulterant. The institute said staff add an extraction solution to powdered samples so the DNA can be replicated. After further processing, authentic samples glow orange under ultraviolet light. The procedure takes less than a day, compared with three days under the traditional DNA test.

Assistant Director of Health (Chinese Medicine) Dr Darwin Mak said the method cuts both time and cost and should help quality control. He said the institute has also developed a chemical-marker protocol for compound Chinese medicine granules, which contain several herbs that previously had to be tested one by one. The new protocol can assess multiple markers across different formulations at the same time.

The institute’s permanent building in Tseung Kwan O began operating in phases late last year. The government said it covers about 27,000 square metres and houses four advanced laboratories, including an electronic sensory system known as an electronic tongue. A pilot project is using that system to digitise the taste of Chinese medicines so identification methods can later draw on taste data.

Federation of the Hong Kong Chinese Medicine Practitioners and Chinese Medicine Traders Association president Tommy Li said judging herbs only by experience or appearance can lead to mistakes, and that microscopic identification saves time and money. He said testing companies routinely take up methods developed by the institute, which then reach firms that do not run their own laboratories.

zh.headline: 中藥檢測中心：鹿茸鑑定可縮至一日內
zh.dek: 衞生署政府中藥檢測中心表示，新的DNA方法可在一日內分辨鹿茸飲片是否正品，較傳統檢測約三天為短。
body: 政府星期日介紹，衞生署政府中藥檢測中心自2017年成立以來，已完成22個專題研究，其中包括一套快速DNA方法，用以鑑定鹿茸飲片是否來自正品。
按照《中國藥典》，只有梅花鹿或馬鹿的鹿茸才列為正品，其他品種會被視為偽品。中心表示，化驗人員會在鹿茸粉末樣本加入提取液，複製並擴增當中的DNA；經特定程序處理後，正品樣本在紫外光下會呈現橙色。整項程序可在一日內完成，傳統DNA檢測則約需三天。
衞生署助理署長（中醫藥）麥懷禮表示，新方法可同時節省時間和成本，有助加強品質控制。他說，近年中藥複方顆粒愈見普遍，以往每種藥材都要分開檢測；中心研發的化學指標分析方法通用性較高，可一次過評估不同處方的多項指標成分。
中心位於將軍澳的永久大樓由去年年底起分期啟用，樓面面積約2.7萬平方米，設有四間高端實驗室，其中包括俗稱「電子舌」的電子感官分析系統。中心已展開先導計劃，嘗試把中藥味道數碼化，建立味感數據庫，以便日後以味道數據協助鑑定。
香港中醫中藥界聯合總會會長李應生表示，單靠經驗或外觀鑑定藥材容易混淆，顯微鑑定可更有效分辨真偽，並節省時間和金錢。他說，檢測公司會採用中心開發的技術，沒有自設實驗室的中藥企業亦會受惠。
